proposals.title: Correct CanonicalEncoder intrinsic capture, ADR-009 consistency, and evidence completeness
proposals.why_now: Three consecutive review rejections (TASK-0004, TASK-0005, TASK-0006) all cite the identical two blockers: mutable ambient built-ins read at encoding time rather than captured at module initialization, and missing independently captured npm run compile and npm run boundary output. A focused fix of these two issues, plus resolving the ADR-009 internal contradiction on Set subclasses and ensuring monkeypatch tests actually reach the patched code paths, is the minimum work required to unblock FASE-1. Nothing else in FASE-1 can produce a StateHash until the encoder is accepted.

acceptance_targets: ADR-002 in docs/decisions/ specifies the hash function algorithm bit-by-bit with enough detail for byte-identical reimplementation: either SplitMix64 applied to an FNV-1a accumulator of the arguments, or an alternative with equivalent justification; the ADR names which PRNG and which accumulator hash function and defines the mixing steps numerically

ADR-004 in docs/decisions/ specifies the concrete technical mechanism that makes calling division without an explicit rounding mode a build-time error (type-level wrapper, a lint rule keyed on a banned pattern, or a mandatory last parameter with no default), and names which rule or type constraint enforces it
No numeric parameter with economic effect is introduced in either ADR; those belong in a versioned config file per §19

proposals.title: Write ADR-002 (hash function) and ADR-004 (rounding-mode enforcement)
proposals.why_now: ADR-002 and ADR-004 are both DEFINIR items required before the rest of packages/core can be implemented. ADR-002 must specify the hash function bit-by-bit so that the positional RNG is deterministic across platforms (INV-19). ADR-004 must specify how calling division without a declared mode is made a compile-time or lint error. Both are pure document work that does not depend on the CanonicalEncoder being accepted and can proceed in parallel with IDEA-001.

proposals.title: Implement packages/core: branded numeric types, positional RNG, and division helpers
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the root of the §14.5 dependency graph. Every other package depends on it. Without it, the ledger (INV-04 to INV-07), the price generator (INV-02, INV-03), and the tick loop cannot exist. The branded types enforce ADR-003 at the type level; the RNG implements ADR-002; the division helpers implement ADR-004. Once IDEA-001 and IDEA-002 are accepted, core is the natural next unit of work.

proposals.title: Electron main skeleton: security config, preload allowlist, simulation worker, and minimal installer
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance requires the simulation worker to be running out of the renderer thread with a typed message contract, Electron security config matching INV-29, and a minimal installer for Windows and Linux. This work is independent of the domain logic and can proceed in parallel with IDEA-003. Delivering the installer early surfaces ABI and packaging problems before the last week, which the spec explicitly warns against in §14.6.

proposals.title: Implement packages/world: two-asset price generator with two noise layers
proposals.why_now: The price generator is the first domain-neutral module that produces observable, testable output: INV-02 (direct tick lookup equals tick-by-tick advance) and INV-03 (player actions do not alter world price). With packages/core accepted, the world generator can be built and its two most important invariants can be put under automated test. This is the earliest point in FASE-1 where the determinism contract becomes measurable rather than structural.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo infrastructure is complete: workspace config, strict TypeScript, ESLint determinism rules, boundary checker, and CI pipeline are all in place and passing. Every package source file is a single-line empty stub (export {}). No ADRs have been written. The CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009 prerequisite) has been attempted in TASK-0004, TASK-0005, and TASK-0006, all rejected for the same two recurring issues: mutable globals read at call time instead of module init, and absence of independently captured npm run compile and npm run boundary output. Idea cycles 043-049 produced no proposals.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: CanonicalEncoder not accepted after three consecutive rejections, blocking all StateHash-dependent FASE-1 work. The two recurring rejection causes are technically straightforward: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and companion built-ins must be captured at module initialization, and compile/boundary evidence must be verbatim captured output rather than summarized claims.

warnings: The CanonicalEncoder has been rejected across three task attempts (TASK-0004, TASK-0005, TASK-0006) for the same two issues each time. The evidence requirement (verbatim captured compile/boundary output rather than summarized claims) is procedural and must be satisfied by the submission format, not just by running the commands locally. Implementers should treat it as a mandatory evidence artifact, not as an implicit pass.

Idea cycles 043 through 049 produced empty proposal payloads. This ideation gap means the benchmark has been in a heartbeat-only state for several hours with no work proposed. The root cause appears to be the CanonicalEncoder blocking all visible FASE-1 progress; IDEA-004 (Electron skeleton) is deliberately independent of the encoder and should be proposed as parallel work.

ADR-009 had an internal self-contradiction on Set subclasses found during TASK-0005 review. The contradiction is within the team-authored ADR, not in CICLO_SPEC.md, so it does not need a SPEC_BLOCKERS.md entry. It must be resolved in the ADR text and implementation consistently before the next encoder submission.
